title: Deeper/broader cross-peer failure classes, AcDs name-folding, and FreeCAD build boundary
mode: primary-source research and read-only plan refinement
scope: Refresh exact cross-peer DWG/DXF parser and writer failure classes
Check the local AcDs segment-name normalization path against ODA section 24.2.1
Clarify current FreeCAD development-build dependencies and the platform evidence boundary
Refine existing implementation/test owners without expanding per-slice validation

method.kind: Read official upstream release notes, issue reports, specification text, and local parser/test source
method.limitations: The local ODA PDF specified by AGENTS.md was not present at ~/doc/dwg/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf. The ODA-hosted PDF was reviewed read-only for §24.2.1 canonical segment names; no parser behavior was changed. Any future DWG layout change must still consult the authoritative local copy and a sample trace. Mutable peer pages and issue reports are not local reproductions or support evidence.

sources.revision: 0.14.1 NEWS section and current advisory index reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: Release notes enumerate capacity/logical-length drift, stale pointers across realloc, offset and size arithmetic errors, non-finite writer hangs, resource/no-progress issues, and sanitizer/fuzz-discovered memory and cleanup faults. These are hazards in LibreDWG paths, not proof of the same defect in libdxfrw.

The issue index separates culture-sensitive codepage lookup, recursive DXF parser stack exhaustion, per-application EED size overflow/loss, and nested-block deep-copy complexity/stack use. Issue thresholds are peer-specific and do not define format limits.

The section lists canonical segment names as six-byte lowercase spellings: segidx, datidx, _data_, schidx, schdat, search, and blob01. It does not state that uppercase/mixed-case variants are normative or accepted.

The open issue reports an ASan out-of-range POLYFACE face-index read in dxf-g; the open PR proposes a >=1 lower bound that conflicts with negative DXF face-index visibility semantics. No hostile-input execution was performed.
The announcement separates LGPL core exchange formats from commercial DXF and ACIS SAT/SAB components; stock OCCT/FreeCAD is not itself an open-source ACIS reader by implication.

The page describes main as development for FreeCAD 1.2 and specifies C++23, Python 3.11+, Qt 6.4, and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS as its stated build baseline. This is build guidance, not a runtime or DXF acceptance result.

assessment.planImpact: Refines existing PAR-14/PAR-20/PAR-26/PAR-37/PAR-49, 7BE, 7S, and S8 owners. The local AcDs case-folding path remains a compatibility question rather than a confirmed defect because the ODA-listed canonical names are lowercase and no valid uppercase producer/profile was established. Current FreeCAD development dependencies must be bound to the exact target build/platform at the existing composed gate.

implementationReadyChecks: Keep the implementation queue moving; peer vulnerabilities refine only their corresponding local owners and do not establish matching libdxfrw defects.
Do not change DWG byte parsing until the repository-authoritative local ODA section and a real sample trace are reviewed.
Treat the existing lowercase AcDs segment-name handling as canonical; only implement deterministic ASCII case folding if a supported compatibility profile explicitly requires case variants.

If AcDs variant support is selected, add a short generated child-process locale test to the existing DataStorage boundary owner and verify kind/index/payload identity plus a following-record sentinel.

Pin FreeCAD release versus development main, exact build/dependencies, OS/architecture, converter, importer backend, and file hashes at the composed platform gate; unavailable environments are NOT_RUN.
Maintain the fast per-slice validation cadence; leave full suites, peer matrices, sanitizers/fuzzing, and native Linux/Windows GUI work at scheduled/composed checkpoints.
Keep J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 DEFERRED_EXTERNAL; none of these sources supplies their independent semantic or platform evidence.
